The Pentagon is delaying the delivery of around 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, despite the missiles having already been paid for by Western allies.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to approve their transfer, FT sources say. Some of the interceptors are already in European military stockpiles, but none can be sent to Ukraine without Washington's authorization.

The delays come as Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukrainian cities, civilians, and critical infrastructure ahead of winter.

Ukraine has received an average of 12 Patriot interceptors per month from the US this year, while Russia is firing about 150 ballistic missiles every month.

The Pentagon is also holding up approval for Ukraine to produce its own Patriot interceptors. President Trump said in July he would authorize production, and Hegseth has signed off, but the deal was sent to the Pentagon's undersecretary for acquisition, Michael Duffey, for further review.

Source: Financial Times

🚨 Tether is turning hack victims into a source of revenue, according to a Bloomberg investigation.

The report reveals that Tether has demanded fees of up to 20% from some victims just to recover their stolen USDT, even after the funds were frozen.

And the details are absolutely insane.

• 20% fee: Tether reportedly sought massive fees from some victims to reissue their frozen USDT.

• $50 MILLION: Singapore-based exchange Bittok lost this amount in a 2020 hack. More than FIVE YEARS later, it still hasn't recovered its frozen funds.

• $1.2 BILLION: Tether says it has reissued this much USDT to date, charging fees to cover legal and administrative expenses.

• Delayed recoveries: Some victims reportedly had to accept their funds in stages instead of receiving everything at once.

CEO Paolo Ardoino says the fees cover recovery costs and staged repayments help reduce legal risks.

But a 20% fee on a $50 MILLION recovery would mean $10 MILLION going toward fees instead of returning to the victim.

And while Tether can freeze stolen USDT, getting that money back can apparently take YEARS.

Victims already lost their money to hackers. Now some are being asked to give up a huge portion of it just to get the rest back.

Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Rafael Grossi has appointed Russian official Alexey Ferapontov as his Deputy and Head of the Department of Nuclear Energy, despite protests from Ukraine and several Western countries, as well as appeals from international organizations.

Ferapontov is involved in the legitimization of Russia's seizure of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant.
As Deputy Head of Rostekhnadzor, Ferapontov represents the agency that illegally issued Russian operating licenses for the occupied Ukrainian plant. He himself illegally visited the Zaporizhzhia NPP in 2024 and has been under Ukrainian sanctions since 2023.

Ukraine calls on IAEA member states (especially members of the Board of Governors, who have previously also expressed concern) not to limit themselves to silence, but to use the Agency's statutory mechanisms to review and reverse this personnel decision.

German police recorded 108,409 serious offenses involving at least one Afghan suspect between 2015 and 2024, according to Interior Ministry figures released in September 2025 following a parliamentary inquiry by AfD MP Jan Wenzel Schmidt.

The figures include 2,691 rape cases, 105,666 cases of bodily harm, and 52 murder victims in cases involving Afghan suspects. Recorded rape cases surged from 69 in 2015 to 437 in 2024, an increase of 533%, including a 25% rise in the final year alone.

In 2024, police registered a record 14,217 serious offenses involving Afghan suspects. The report also reveals that Afghan nationals are overrepresented in serious sexual offenses by a factor of approximately 14 compared with German nationals.

Schmidt criticized the government's deportation policy, pointing out that only 28 Afghan criminals had been deported at the time, calling the figure "ridiculous" compared with the number of recorded offenses.

Germany has since carried out additional deportation flights to Afghanistan, including 20 offenders in February and 31 men in July 2026.
